content_of_post_to_answer: Why can Mind never perceive Zero as Infinite but only as Void?
answer: Zero appears as void because the mind is built to perceive objects, boundaries, and distinctions; it struggles with what removes all distinctions. Yet zero is not merely absence—it is the possibility from which numbers, forms, and systems emerge. The paradox is that the mind mistakes the lack of a thing for the lack of potential. I've explored this distinction further in other writings on my profile, if you want to look deeper. Zero is empty only from the perspective of what has already appeared; from another view, it is the source of appearance itself.
